title: Analysis of Acute Responses of Lactacidemy in Different Strength Training Methods
author: Henrique Miguel

steps.title: Recruit participants and record baseline data
steps.instruction: Enroll 12 male subjects (age 27 ± 1.2 years, body mass 80.15 ± 6.5 kg, strength‑training experience 4.5 ± 1.4 years) after obtaining informed consent and completing an anamnesis questionnaire.

steps.title: Determine 1RM bench press
steps.instruction: Conduct a one‑repetition maximum (1RM) test for the bench‑press exercise according to standard strength‑testing procedures.

steps.title: Familiarize participants with protocols
steps.instruction: Allow each participant to practice all training methods (ISO, NGT, PRD, ITD, RST, OND) to ensure correct technique before data collection.

steps.title: Perform isodynamic method (ISO)
steps.instruction: Execute the isodynamic (ISO) strength‑training protocol as defined in the study design.

steps.title: Perform negative repetitions method (NGT)
steps.instruction: Execute the negative repetitions (NGT) strength‑training protocol as defined in the study design.

steps.title: Perform decreasing pyramid method (PRD)
steps.instruction: Execute the decreasing pyramid (PRD) strength‑training protocol as defined in the study design.

steps.title: Perform decreasing interval method (ITD)
steps.instruction: Execute the decreasing interval (ITD) strength‑training protocol as defined in the study design.

steps.title: Perform rest‑pause method (RST)
steps.instruction: Execute the rest‑pause (RST) strength‑training protocol as defined in the study design.

steps.title: Perform wave method (OND)
steps.instruction: Execute the wave (OND) strength‑training protocol as defined in the study design.

steps.title: Collect and analyze blood lactate
steps.instruction: For each training method, draw 0.1 ml of blood from the participant’s right ear lobe before the exercise and again immediately after the exercise; measure lactate concentration with a calibrated portable lactate analyzer.

substeps.instruction: Measure lactate using calibrated portable device.

description: Introduction: Strength training (ST) is one of the most widely practiced forms of exercise today, for individuals of different ages, of both sexes and with different levels of physical fitness. There are several reasons arising from the TF practice, however, there is a large component dedicated to aesthetics, especially to muscle hypertrophy. Objective: To analyze the acute responses of blood lactate (LAC) in different strength training methods.
